prompt: By this lesson's rule, where does a database password that should change every thirty days go?

choices.text: Secrets Manager

choices.text: Parameter Store, as a String

choices.text: An environment variable in the image
choices.why: Then it is in every copy of the image.

choices.text: A file in the repository, encrypted

prompt: Without --with-decryption, moto returned 'kms:alias/aws/ssm:first-pass' for a SecureString. What does AWS return?
hint: The lab called it moto's idea of encryption.

choices.text: The same, with the plaintext after the key name
choices.why: Then anybody could read it; that is moto only.

choices.text: An empty string
choices.why: It returns the encrypted value.

choices.text: KMS ciphertext, unreadable without the key
choices.why: Right. Decrypting needs permission on the key as well.

choices.text: An access-denied error
choices.why: Reading the encrypted value is allowed by ssm:GetParameter.

prompt: To replace the value of an existing parameter, put-parameter needs the flag --____. (one word)
What is the largest value, in KB, a standard parameter may hold on AWS?
A policy names arn:aws:secretsmanager:sa-east-1:123456789012:secret:shop/prod/db exactly, with no wildcard. What goes wrong on AWS?
hint: Look at the end of the secret's real ARN.

choices.text: Nothing; Secrets Manager ignores the suffix
choices.why: The ARN carries the suffix and the policy must match it.

choices.text: A six-character suffix
choices.why: Right. The real ARN ends with six random characters, hence secret:shop/prod/db-*.

choices.text: It matches every secret under shop/prod
choices.why: Without a wildcard it matches one string exactly.

choices.text: It is refused when the policy is saved
choices.why: The policy is valid; it just names nothing that exists.

prompt: Match each staging label to what it marks.

pairs.right: What a read without a stage returns
The version before the current one
A new value a rotation has not finished

prompt: Put the four steps of a rotation function in order.
moto rotated a secret with no function and the next read failed. Which real bug does that resemble?
hint: Which step must never run without the others?

choices.text: Moving the stage too early
choices.why: Right. AWSCURRENT moved before a value was set: the one bug a rotation function must not have.

choices.text: A function that runs every day instead of monthly
choices.why: Frequent rotation is safe if each one completes.

choices.text: A function that tests the new password
choices.why: Testing is step three, and the safeguard.

choices.text: A secret replicated to another region
choices.why: Replication is unrelated to the stage.

prompt: How many days does a deleted secret wait by default before it is gone?
hint: The DeletionDate was a month away.

prompt: In cache-demo.py, why did the read just after the change return the old password?

choices.text: Secrets Manager takes a minute to store a new version
choices.why: The new version was there; the program did not ask.

choices.text: put_secret_value made the new version AWSPENDING
choices.why: It became AWSCURRENT at once.

choices.text: The fingerprint hides the change
choices.why: The fingerprint changed three seconds later.

choices.text: The cache was still fresh; no call was made
choices.why: Right. Three reads, two calls.

prompt: 10 containers each read a secret every 5 minutes for a 30-day month. How many calls is that?
What should a log line about a secret carry, by this lesson?

choices.text: The secret's value, masked after the first characters
choices.why: The first characters of a password are part of the password.

choices.text: Nothing at all about the secret
choices.why: A fingerprint is useful and safe.

choices.text: A fingerprint, the start of its SHA-256
choices.why: Right. It shows a change without showing the value.

choices.text: The value, base64-encoded
choices.why: Base64 is an encoding, not a protection.

prompt: What does INITIAL_NO_AUTH_ACTION_COUNT=9 tell moto to do?

choices.text: Refuse the first nine requests
choices.why: It is the opposite.

choices.text: Allow nine users
choices.why: It counts requests, not users.

choices.text: Retry each failed request nine times
choices.why: It has nothing to do with retries.

choices.text: Let nine requests through, then check policies
choices.why: Right. Every request counts, a mistyped one included.

prompt: Under moto, shop-app's correct, narrow policy was refused on its own secret. Why?

choices.text: moto matches every request against *, never an ARN
choices.why: Right. On AWS the same policy allows the read.

choices.text: The suffix wildcard is invalid

choices.text: Access keys take a minute to work

prompt: Which requests does AWS allow? Choose all that apply.

choices.why: Yes; moto refused it, AWS allows it.

choices.text: shop-wide reads shop/prod/payments

choices.why: No ssm action is granted.

choices.why: No statement allows PutSecretValue.

choices.text: shop-app reads shop/prod/payments
